messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: high error rate after rollout. Service: api-gateway. Trigger: deploy 2026-02-19T15:20Z to prod-us-east. Paging on-call.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-02-19T15:18Z => release/rls/feature-search-v42 started canary in us-east-2 (10% traffic)
ed_oncall: I'm on it, paging db-sre and release owner. Seeing a spike in 500s on /v1/generate (latency also up).
alice.k: I can confirm increased 5xx from CloudFront logs, error is DB: "ERROR: deadlock found when trying to get lock" and also a few "column \"customer_tier\" does not exist" in app logs.
carol_sre: @ed_oncall, @ben.r paging — symptoms look like simultaneous schema mismatch + long migrations locking tables. I see ALTER TABLE add column jobs in the release task logs. Was the migration supposed to be online?
ben.r: That migration was added to release: add customer_tier text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free' — intended to be backfilled async, but I think the deploy ran the heavy backfill in-process. My bad, oversight in migration settings.
ed_oncall: Attach logs: ```
2026-02-19T15:21:10Z app[worker]: applying migration 20260219_add_customer_tier
2026-02-19T15:21:11Z db[primary]: ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN customer_tier text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free';
2026-02-19T15:21:11Z db[primary]: LOCK TABLE accounts; -- waiting
2026-02-19T15:22:05Z app[web]: 500 "column \"customer_tier\" does not exist" at users/42
```
carol_sre: That sequence explains both errors: some app replicas pulled new code expecting the column, while primary was in mid-migration causing locks and transient missing-column errors on replicas that are running older schema code. We need to stop the rollout and reduce blast radius.
dave_release: I'm the release owner — initiating immediate kill-switch on the feature flag and will pause the canary. Toggling now.
dave_release: @deploy-bot can you pause traffic for release/rls/feature-search-v42 and demote canary to 0%?
deploy-bot: Command acknowledged. Pausing canary and routing traffic away from canary hosts. New traffic split applied: 100% stable, 0% rls/feature-search-v42.
alice.k: Confirming 5xx rate dropped ~70% within one minute after pause, but DB locks persist. Some background jobs are still running the migration.
carol_sre: Next step: stop migration processes on app side to release DB locks. @ben.r can you coordinate with infra to SIGTERM any migration worker instances? We should avoid abrupt DB kills; prefer graceful stop so backfill can finish later offline.
ben.r: I'm removing migration job trigger from the release manifest and scaling migration job to 0. Pushing change to k8s batch controller: ```kubectl scale job migration-job-20260219 --replicas=0 -n prod```
ben.r: Executed. I see the migration job shutting down, DB locks are being released. Monitoring.
ed_oncall: DB lock count down from 12 to 0, replication lag normalizing. App 5xxs down to baseline. Good.
carol_sre: OK, immediate mitigation successful. Now we need rollback strategy and customer impact assessment. @dave_release, do you want a full rollback of the deploy or just revert migration-related pieces and re-roll with safe migration path?
dave_release: Full rollback of code that expects new column to prevent any lingering incompatibility. We'll re-deploy stable, then schedule a proper 0-downtime migration: ADD COLUMN NULL, backfill in batches, then ALTER SET NOT NULL. Target a controlled maintenance window.
alice.k: Systems impacted: API requests to document-generation and user-profile endpoints — approx 3.7% of total requests showed 5xx during the 4-minute window before the kill-switch. Affected customers: spikes in error budgets for a subset of enterprise customers routed to us-east-2. No data corruption detected.
carol_sre: Filing incident ticket in PagerDuty with severity-high and creating follow-up tasks: rollback, migration remediation plan, postmortem. @alice.k can you attach request traces and sampling of error logs to the ticket?
alice.k: On it. Collected traces + representative stack traces: ```
TraceID: f1a2b3 - 500 at /v1/dispatch - root cause: missing column
TraceID: f1a2b4 - 502 at /v1/generate - root cause: db lock timeout
```
ben.r: I've kicked off rollback to the stable image tag (stable-20260218) and monitoring deploy. deploy-bot reports rollout started to revert canary hosts.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated. Rolling back pods in us-east-2: 15 pods updated. Health checks passing on 8/15, waiting for remaining.
ed_oncall: Handing off on-call to carol_sre for ongoing DB watch and post-rollback checks. I'm staying reachable for customer comms.
carol_sre: On-call acknowledged. I'll monitor DB locks, replication, and queue depths for the next 2 hours. If anything regresses, page the DB pager.
alice.k: Customer comms draft ready: short note explaining temporary rollout error, immediate mitigation (feature flag kill-switch + rollback), no customer data loss, mitigation steps, ETA for permanent fix. Ready for review: "We briefly serviced increased errors due to a schema migration running during a partial rollout. We paused the rollout and rolled back code; we are scheduling a safe migration window."
dave_release: Approving comms. Please send to customers impacted via status page and email for enterprise contacts. Also prepare a postmortem runbook with timeline and action items.
carol_sre: Immediate action items assigned: 1) migration remediation plan (ben.r), 2) add deploy-time block for non-online migrations (dave_release), 3) improve preflight checks for schema+code sync (alice.k). Will followup with owner assignments in ticket.
ben.r: Root cause: migration ran as blocking ALTER with NOT NULL/default in same release; no guard to prevent schema-changing jobs from running during canary traffic. Fix plan: split migration into incremental safe steps, add CI gate to detect non-online alters in PRs.
ed_oncall: Closing timeline note: incident opened 2026-02-19T15:20Z; kill-switch at ~15:22Z; rollback started 15:24Z; errors back to baseline 15:26Z. Total customer-impact window ~6 minutes peak. Will create timeline in postmortem doc.
carol_sre: I'll keep thread open for 2 hours for any regression. Tagging this as incident/mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:
